title: Extend Windows teardown timeout to 5s for native library handle release
context: Test teardown fails on Windows when spawned child processes hold file handles on fixtures. Previous approach (1 second of retry) was insufficient for native tree-sitter/sqlite handles to release, causing EPERM errors that mask regressions in adjacent code. Touches invariant(s): con_7217ab24ab (Regression guard: "Flaky test failure under parallelism: native tree-sitter module resolution race on Windows" must not recur.).
decision: Increase retry budget from 10 × 100ms to 20 × 250ms (5 seconds total) in a centralized cleanupDir() helper. Rethrow after retries expire to ensure persistent leaks are still detected, not silently ignored.
consequences: Worst-case teardown latency increases from ~1s to ~5s when handles are actually held
Eliminates false-negative test failures that masked regressions in shared-mode publishing, merge, and memory-pump code
Centralizing to helpers.ts prevents code duplication and drift (OVERLAY_IGNORE precedent)
alternatives_rejected: Accept 1-second timeout and skip the test on Windows — loses coverage
Use async cleanup — node:test does not support async teardown hooks
Silently ignore EPERM in teardown — masks real handle leaks
Keep separate implementations per test file — invites inconsistency and divergence
